# Pulse

> A lightweight macOS memory monitor for quickly understanding why a Mac feels slow and deciding which app to close.

Pulse is an open-source native macOS menu bar utility built in SwiftUI. It shows real-time system memory pressure and the largest running apps, then lets users quit or force quit an app quickly. It is designed for the moment a Mac feels slow—not as a replacement for Activity Monitor's deep CPU, disk, network, and process diagnostics.

## When Pulse Is Useful
- A Mac feels slow and you want a fast view of memory pressure.
- You want to identify the largest running apps by resident memory and quit one without opening a full system utility.
- You want to open Pulse from anywhere with `Command + Option + P`.

For exact Chrome tab/process memory, Chrome's built-in Task Manager (`Shift + Escape`) is the authoritative source. Pulse lists open Chrome tabs but does not invent unreliable per-tab RAM totals.

## Quick Installation
Run in terminal:
`curl -fsSL https://pulse0.app/install.sh | bash`

Direct DMG download:
https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse/releases/latest/download/Pulse.dmg

## Core Capabilities
- **Real-Time Memory Telemetry**: Direct kernel page reading via Mach host statistics (`host_statistics64`), identical to `vm_stat`.
- **System Memory Pressure**: Hardware pressure source monitoring (`DispatchSource.makeMemoryPressureSource`) tracking Low, Medium, and High pressure states.
- **Process Memory Aggregation**: Uses `proc_pid_rusage` resident-memory measurements to group helper processes under their parent application without presenting summed process footprints as total system RAM.
- **Google Chrome Tab Inspection**: Lists open tabs for review. Exact per-tab/process memory is available in Chrome Task Manager (`Shift + Escape`).
- **Instant Force Quit**: Holding the ⌥ Option key dynamically converts Quit actions into kernel-level `SIGKILL` (`NSRunningApplication.forceTerminate()`).
- **Minimal Overhead**: Designed to stay out of the way as a native menu-bar app.
